html:
The Kingdom of Burundi was a monarchy in the hills east of Lake Tanganyika, founded in about the late 17th century and lasting until 1966.

Its king, the mwami, ruled through princes of the royal line, the ganwa, who stood above both Tutsi and Hutu. Power rested on cattle, land and sacred rituals, among them the royal drums. Like its neighbour the Kingdom of Rwanda, it shared one language, Kirundi.

Mwezi IV resisted German rule before accepting it. Under the Germans and then Belgium the monarchy survived, and it reached independence in 1962. A coup in 1966 abolished it, and power passed to Tutsi army officers.
sum: The Kingdom of Burundi was a monarchy in the hills east of Lake Tanganyika, founded in about the late 17th century and lasting until 1966.
